scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Shamanic Possession Dance of Assam
This is Deodhani. Traditional.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Deodhani is a shaman folk dance from the Indian state of Assam, of Bodo origin.
The name derives from 'Deo' (God) and 'Dhani' (woman), literally meaning a woman possessed by god.
A male shaman form is also present, called 'Deodha-Joki' in Kamrup by the Bodo people and 'Deodhai' elsewhere in Assam.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance form is associated with the worship of the snake goddess Marei/Maroi, depicting possession by a spiritual being.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: It can be performed either solo or in a group, with group performances generally consisting of three or four women.
Dancers take a sword and shield and present a virile war dance during the performance, depicting the dance of a shaman woman or man when possessed by a spiritual being.
Watch for Virile war dance with sword and shield.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is generally performed to the accompaniment of songs sung by an Ojha, a traditional chorus leader in the Darrang district of Assam.
These songs sung by Ojapali are known as Xuknoni in undivided Darrang district, whereas in undivided Kamrup district it is accompanied by Kamrupi Bor-Dhol's.
Listen for the Kamrupi Bor-Dhol.
Accompanied by traditional chorus songs called Xuknoni sung by an Ojha or Kamrupi Bor-Dhol drums.
